title: Behold! my first time dev, ai/human error Jank!
author: Skumby73
selftext:
I've been teaching myself Godot by building a sci-fi survival RPG called Nulltide.

The original goal was pretty simple: crash on a strange island, build a settlement, explore dangerous locations, and uncover what happened to the world.

Since then it's grown into settlement management, worker cloning, crafting, research, expeditions, procedural gear, combat, and a growing list of systems that seemed like good ideas at the time.

It's still very early. Most of the visuals are placeholders, the balance is all over the place, and I'm focusing on making the systems work before I spend a lot of time polishing things. Right now I'm more interested in finding out what's fun than making everything pretty.

I've also been using AI heavily throughout development. Mostly for programming assistance, debugging, brainstorming, documentation, and helping me move faster as a solo developer. It's been surprisingly useful, though it occasionally helps me create problems I didn't have five minutes earlier.

Here's some screenshots.

https://preview.redd.it/5iz038jzfd4h1.png?width=1009&format=png&auto=webp&s=ddfc5ac99068430b34606e51e6ccb7fdc5b997c5

https://preview.redd.it/84ne5k21gd4h1.png?width=1111&format=png&auto=webp&s=a3b0591e6df00d8a1bf884947c49290e844fd145

Feedback on the game is welcome too. Just remember you're looking at a very rough prototype and not a finished product. [Nulltide on Itch.io](https://sko0.itch.io/nulltide)



I'm curious what other AI-assisted developers are working on and what tools you've found genuinely useful. Most of the discussion I see is about generating assets, but I've gotten far more mileage out of AI helping me build systems and untangle my own code.
